category: Graphics > Specialized Charts, Animation, Annotation Lines & Interaction
description: Base MATLAB graphics functions not covered by the core plotting files: animation (animatedline, getframe, movie), specialized statistical and multivariable charts, 3-D and volume plots, reference lines and regions, color order, data tips, interactive exploration and graphics-object utilities.

tools.name: animatedline
tools.description: Creates an animated line object to which points can be appended efficiently inside a loop, instead of replotting the whole line each iteration. It is the recommended way to draw streaming or progressively computed data.
tools.usage:
an = animatedline
an = animatedline(x, y)
an = animatedline(x, y, z)
an = animatedline(ax, ___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: MaximumNumPoints
parameters.description: Maximum points kept; oldest points are discarded (default 1000000).

tools.notes: Use drawnow limitrate to cap the refresh rate at 20 fps for speed. Retrieve data with getpoints and clear with clearpoints. Set MaximumNumPoints for a scrolling strip-chart.

tools.name: addpoints
tools.description: Appends one or more data points to the end of an animated line created with animatedline. Call drawnow afterwards to display the new points.
tools.usage:
addpoints(an, x, y)
addpoints(an, x, y, z)

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: Scalar or vector coordinates of the new points (same length).

tools.notes: Adding points in batches (vectors) is faster than one at a time. Works only with animatedline, not with Line objects from plot.

tools.name: comet
tools.description: Plots data as an animated comet: a head marker traces the path while a short tail follows it. Useful for visualizing trajectories and the time order of 2-D data.
tools.usage:
comet(y)
comet(x, y)
comet(x, y, p)
comet(ax, ___)

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Tail length as a fraction of the data length (default 0.1).

tools.example:
t = linspace(0, 4*pi, 800);
comet(t.*cos(t), t.*sin(t), 0.05)
tools.notes: comet3 animates 3-D trajectories. The animation speed depends on the number of points; for controlled timing use animatedline with pause.

tools.name: getframe
tools.description: Captures the current axes or figure as a movie frame (a struct with cdata image data and colormap). Frames are used to build movies, write videos with VideoWriter or save animated GIFs.
tools.usage:
F = getframe
F = getframe(ax)
F = getframe(fig)
F = getframe(___, rect)

parameters.name: ax / fig
parameters.description: Axes or figure to capture (default current axes).

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: [left bottom width height] region in pixels relative to the target.

tools.example:
v = VideoWriter("wave.mp4", "MPEG-4"); open(v)
for k = 1:60
    plot(sin((1:100)/10 + k/5)); ylim([-1 1])
    writeVideo(v, getframe(gcf));
end
close(v)
tools.notes: The window must be visible and on-screen for reliable captures; for headless export use exportgraphics or print. Frame size depends on screen DPI. Convert with frame2im for image processing or GIF writing.

tools.name: movie
tools.description: Plays back an array of movie frames captured with getframe in the current figure or axes, optionally repeating and at a chosen frame rate.
tools.usage:
movie(M)
movie(M, n)
movie(M, n, fps)
movie(h, ___)

parameters.name: M
parameters.description: Array of frame structs from getframe.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of times to play (default 1); a vector lists frame order.

tools.example:
for k = 1:20
    surf(peaks(30) * sin(k*pi/10)); zlim([-10 10])
    M(k) = getframe;
end
movie(M, 3, 24)
tools.notes: For files, write the frames with VideoWriter instead. Preallocate M with struct('cdata',[],'colormap',[]) for long captures.

tools.name: frame2im
tools.description: Converts a movie frame from getframe into an image array (RGB truecolor or indexed with colormap). Use it to process captured frames or write animated GIF files with imwrite.
tools.usage:
RGB = frame2im(F)
[X, map] = frame2im(F)

parameters.name: F
parameters.description: Single frame struct with cdata and colormap fields.

tools.notes: im2frame performs the reverse conversion. Since R2022a exportgraphics(..., Append=true) can also build animated GIFs directly.

tools.name: stackedplot
tools.description: Plots the variables of a table or timetable (or the columns of a matrix) in vertically stacked axes that share a common x-axis. Ideal for comparing multiple sensor channels over time.
tools.usage:
stackedplot(tbl)
stackedplot(tbl, vars)
stackedplot(X)
stackedplot(x, Y)
stackedplot(tbl1, ..., tblN)
s = stackedplot(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: Variables to plot; a cell element with several names overlays them in one axes.

parameters.name: XVariable
parameters.description: Table variable used for the x-axis (timetables use row times).

tools.notes: Introduced R2018b; multiple tables/timetables since R2020b. It is a standalone chart: use its properties (AxesProperties, LineProperties) rather than hold/axes functions.

tools.name: bubblechart
tools.description: Creates a bubble chart where marker area encodes a third variable and color optionally a fourth. Bubble sizes are scaled relative to each other within limits set by bubblesize and bubblelim.
tools.usage:
bubblechart(x, y, sz)
bubblechart(x, y, sz, c)
bubblechart(tbl, xvar, yvar, sizevar)
bc = bubblechart(ax, ___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: sz
parameters.description: Bubble size data (relative, mapped to the bubblesize range).

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Color name, RGB triplet or vector mapped to the colormap.

tools.example:
x = rand(20,1); y = rand(20,1); pop = randi([1e3 1e6], 20, 1);
bubblechart(x, y, pop, pop)
bubblesize([5 30])
bubblelegend("Population", Location="eastoutside")
colorbar
tools.notes: Introduced R2020b; table syntax R2021b. bubblechart3 draws 3-D bubbles and geobubble plots bubbles on maps. Unlike scatter, sizes are relative, not in points squared.

tools.name: scatterhistogram
tools.description: Creates a scatter plot with marginal histograms (or kernel density curves) along both axes, optionally grouped by a categorical variable. It shows joint and marginal distributions in one chart.
tools.usage:
scatterhistogram(tbl, xvar, yvar)
scatterhistogram(tbl, xvar, yvar, GroupVariable=grpvar)
scatterhistogram(xvalues, yvalues)
s = scatterhistogram(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: GroupVariable / GroupData
parameters.description: Grouping variable name (table) or grouping vector.

parameters.name: NumBins / LineStyle / MarkerStyle
parameters.description: Histogram bins and appearance per group.

tools.notes: Introduced R2018b. Standalone chart object; cannot be combined with hold on or placed in tiledlayout tiles prior to newer releases.

tools.name: parallelplot
tools.description: Creates a parallel coordinates plot where each observation is a polyline across vertical axes, one per variable. Good for spotting patterns and clusters in multivariate tabular data.
tools.usage:
parallelplot(tbl)
parallelplot(tbl, CoordinateVariables=vars, GroupVariable=g)
parallelplot(data)
p = parallelplot(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: CoordinateVariables
parameters.description: Table variables to use as axes.

parameters.name: GroupVariable / GroupData
parameters.description: Variable or vector used to color lines by group.

tools.notes: Introduced R2019a. Categorical variables are supported as coordinates. For many rows, reduce opacity via LineAlpha.

tools.name: plotmatrix
tools.description: Creates a scatter plot matrix of all pairs of columns, with histograms on the diagonal when a single matrix is given. A quick exploratory view of correlations among variables.
tools.usage:
plotmatrix(X)
plotmatrix(X, Y)
plotmatrix(___, LineSpec)
[S, AX, BigAx, H, HAx] = plotmatrix(___)

parameters.name: X, Y
parameters.description: Matrices; plotmatrix(X,Y) plots columns of Y against columns of X.

tools.notes: For grouped scatter matrices use gplotmatrix (Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox). corrplot (Econometrics) adds correlation coefficients.

tools.name: binscatter
tools.description: Creates a binned scatter plot that aggregates points into rectangular bins colored by count. It is the scalable alternative to scatter for millions of points or tall arrays, and rebins automatically when zooming.
tools.usage:
binscatter(x, y)
binscatter(x, y, N)
binscatter(___, Name=Value)
h = binscatter(___)

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Number of bins, scalar or [nx ny].

tools.notes: Introduced R2017b. Also supports tall arrays. histogram2 with DisplayStyle="tile" gives similar output with explicit edges.

tools.name: wordcloud
tools.description: Creates a word cloud chart where word size reflects frequency or another weight. Accepts a table of words and counts, word and size arrays, or categorical data (counts computed automatically).
tools.usage:
wordcloud(tbl, wordVar, sizeVar)
wordcloud(words, sizeData)
wordcloud(C)
wc = wordcloud(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Color / HighlightColor
parameters.description: Word colors; the largest words use HighlightColor.

tools.notes: Introduced R2017b. Passing raw text, tokenized documents, bag-of-words or LDA models requires Text Analytics Toolbox, which also provides wordCloudCounts.

tools.name: geobubble
tools.description: Creates a geographic bubble chart on a basemap, with bubble size and color encoding data values at latitude/longitude locations. It works in base MATLAB without Mapping Toolbox.
tools.usage:
geobubble(tbl, latvar, lonvar)
geobubble(tbl, latvar, lonvar, SizeVariable=sv, ColorVariable=cv)
geobubble(lat, lon, sizedata, colordata)
gb = geobubble(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: SizeVariable / sizedata
parameters.description: Numeric data mapped to bubble area.

parameters.name: ColorVariable / colordata
parameters.description: Categorical data mapped to bubble color.

tools.notes: Most basemaps require an internet connection; "darkwater" and "landcover" styles ship offline. Introduced R2017b. For general geographic plotting use geoplot/geoscatter.

tools.name: bar3
tools.description: Draws a three-dimensional bar graph of a matrix, one bar per element, with detached, grouped or stacked styles. Useful for showing values over two categorical dimensions.
tools.usage:
bar3(Z)
bar3(y, Z)
bar3(___, width)
bar3(___, style)
b = bar3(___)
tools.notes: Returns Surface objects (one per column); color by height as in the example. bar3h draws horizontal 3-D bars. heatmap is often clearer than 3-D bars.

tools.name: pie3
tools.description: Draws a 3-D pie chart of the values in a vector, optionally offsetting (exploding) slices and labeling them.
tools.usage:
pie3(X)
pie3(X, explode)
pie3(X, labels)
pie3(X, explode, labels)
p = pie3(___)

parameters.name: explode
parameters.description: Logical or numeric vector; nonzero elements offset the slice.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Cell array or string array of slice labels.

tools.notes: If sum(X) < 1, a partial pie is drawn. For 2-D charts use pie or piechart/donutchart (R2023b+).

tools.name: waterfall
tools.description: Creates a waterfall plot: a mesh drawn only along row lines, so each row appears as a curtain-like trace. Common for spectra evolving over time or parameter sweeps.
tools.usage:
waterfall(Z)
waterfall(X, Y, Z)
waterfall(___, C)
h = waterfall(___)

parameters.name: X, Y, Z
parameters.description: Grid coordinates and heights (rows are traces).

tools.notes: Transpose Z to draw curtains along the other dimension. ribbon and plot3 give similar effects; spectrogram(...,'yaxis') is usually better for time-frequency data.

tools.name: ribbon
tools.description: Plots the columns of a matrix as 3-D ribbons of uniform width, each ribbon colored differently. It separates overlapping 2-D lines into depth for easier comparison.
tools.usage:
ribbon(Y)
ribbon(X, Y)
ribbon(X, Y, width)
h = ribbon(___)
tools.notes: Returns Surface objects. For large numbers of series consider stackedplot or waterfall.

tools.name: polarhistogram
tools.description: Creates a histogram in polar coordinates (a rose plot) of angular data in radians. It is the modern replacement for rose, for directions such as wind, phase or orientation.
tools.usage:
polarhistogram(theta)
polarhistogram(theta, nbins)
polarhistogram(theta, edges)
h = polarhistogram(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Introduced R2016b. Convert degrees with deg2rad. Configure the PolarAxes (ThetaZeroLocation, ThetaDir, RLim) for compass-style display.

tools.name: polarscatter
tools.description: Creates a scatter plot in polar coordinates with optional marker size and color data. Use it for antenna samples, directional measurements or any angle/radius data.
tools.usage:
polarscatter(theta, rho)
polarscatter(theta, rho, sz)
polarscatter(theta, rho, sz, c)
polarscatter(___, "filled")
ps = polarscatter(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Introduced R2016b. Also supports table input in newer releases. Use polarplot for lines and polarhistogram for distributions.

tools.name: contour3
tools.description: Creates a 3-D contour plot in which each contour line is drawn at its height in z, giving a layered view of a surface.
tools.usage:
contour3(Z)
contour3(X, Y, Z)
contour3(___, levels)
[M, c] = contour3(___)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Number of levels or vector of level values.

tools.notes: Use contour/contourf for 2-D, surfc to combine a surface with contours below it, and fcontour for function handles.

tools.name: slice
tools.description: Draws orthogonal (or arbitrary surface) slice planes through volumetric data, coloring each plane by the interpolated volume values. Used for CT/MRI volumes, 3-D simulation fields and similar data.
tools.usage:
slice(X, Y, Z, V, xslice, yslice, zslice)
slice(V, xslice, yslice, zslice)
slice(X, Y, Z, V, xq, yq, zq)
slice(___, method)
s = slice(___)

parameters.name: V
parameters.description: 3-D array of volume data on a meshgrid-format grid.

parameters.name: xslice, yslice, zslice
parameters.description: Locations of planes along each axis ([] for none).

parameters.name: xq, yq, zq
parameters.description: Matrices defining a curved slice surface.

tools.notes: Grid must be in meshgrid (not ndgrid) format. Related volume tools: isosurface, contourslice, volshow (Image Processing Toolbox).

tools.name: isosurface
tools.description: Extracts an isosurface (surface of constant value) from volume data as faces and vertices, which are then displayed with patch. Without outputs it draws the surface directly.
tools.usage:
fv = isosurface(X, Y, Z, V, isovalue)
fv = isosurface(V, isovalue)
[faces, verts, colors] = isosurface(X, Y, Z, V, isovalue, colors)
isosurface(___)

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: Array interpolated onto the surface vertices for coloring.

tools.notes: Call isonormals for smooth shading and isocaps to close open ends. reducevolume and reducepatch speed up large volumes.

tools.name: streamslice
tools.description: Draws well-spaced streamlines with direction arrows for 2-D vector fields, or on slice planes of 3-D fields. It gives an automatic, uncluttered view of flow direction.
tools.usage:
streamslice(X, Y, U, V)
streamslice(X, Y, Z, U, V, W, startx, starty, startz)
streamslice(___, density)
streamslice(___, "noarrows")
lines = streamslice(___)
tools.notes: streamline draws lines from explicit start points, quiver draws arrows at grid points.

tools.name: trisurf
tools.description: Plots a triangulated surface from a triangle connectivity list and vertex coordinates, typically produced by delaunay or a mesh generator. Useful for scattered data and FEM meshes.
tools.usage:
trisurf(T, x, y, z)
trisurf(T, x, y, z, c)
trisurf(TO)
h = trisurf(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: trimesh draws only edges and triplot 2-D triangles. For regular grids use surf.

tools.name: delaunay
tools.description: Computes the Delaunay triangulation (2-D) or tetrahedralization (3-D) of a set of points and returns the connectivity list. It is the basis for plotting and interpolating scattered data.
tools.usage:
T = delaunay(x, y)
T = delaunay(x, y, z)
T = delaunay(P)
tools.notes: delaunayTriangulation provides a richer object (nearestNeighbor, pointLocation, constrained edges). Duplicate points are merged.

tools.name: fcontour
tools.description: Plots contour lines of a function z = f(x,y) given as a function handle, adaptively evaluating it over an interval. No manual grid creation is needed.
tools.usage:
fcontour(f)
fcontour(f, xyinterval)
fcontour(___, LineSpec)
fc = fcontour(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function handle of two variables (use element-wise operators) or symbolic expression.

parameters.name: LevelList / Fill / MeshDensity
parameters.description: Contour levels, filled contours ("on") and evaluation density (default 71).

tools.notes: Related function plotters: fplot, fsurf, fmesh, fimplicit, fimplicit3. The handle must be vectorized.

tools.name: fill3
tools.description: Creates filled 3-D polygons from vertex coordinate arrays, one polygon per column. Useful for drawing planes, facets and custom 3-D shapes.
tools.usage:
fill3(X, Y, Z, C)
fill3(X1, Y1, Z1, C1, ..., Xn, Yn, Zn, Cn)
fill3(___, Name=Value)
p = fill3(___)

parameters.name: X, Y, Z
parameters.description: Vertex coordinates; columns define separate polygons.

parameters.name: C
parameters.description: Color name, RGB triplet or color data.

tools.notes: Returns Patch objects; use patch directly for shared vertices (Faces/Vertices).

tools.name: xline
tools.description: Draws vertical reference lines at constant x values that span the axes and stay in place when zooming or panning, with optional text labels. Useful for thresholds, events and markers on time axes.
tools.usage:
xline(x)
xline(x, LineSpec)
xline(x, LineSpec, labels)
xl = xline(ax, ___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Scalar or vector of x positions (numeric, datetime, duration, categorical).

tools.example:
t = 0:0.01:10; plot(t, sin(t))
xline([pi 2*pi 3*pi], "--r", ["\pi" "2\pi" "3\pi"], LabelVerticalAlignment="bottom");
tools.notes: Introduced R2018b; vector input since R2021a. yline draws horizontal lines. Reference lines are excluded from axis limit calculations.

tools.name: yline
tools.description: Draws horizontal reference lines at constant y values, such as limits, set points or mean values, optionally with labels. The lines always span the full x-range of the axes.
tools.usage:
yline(y)
yline(y, LineSpec)
yline(y, LineSpec, labels)
yl = yline(ax, ___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Scalar or vector of y positions.

tools.notes: Introduced R2018b; vectors since R2021a. Use yregion for shaded bands.

tools.name: xregion
tools.description: Shades one or more vertical regions between pairs of x values across the full height of the axes. Use it to highlight time windows, operating ranges or tolerance bands; yregion is the horizontal counterpart.
tools.usage:
xregion(x1, x2)
xregion(X)
xregion(ax, ___)
xr = xregion(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: x1, x2
parameters.description: Region bounds; vectors create several regions. Inf/-Inf allowed (R2023b+).

parameters.name: FaceColor / FaceAlpha / EdgeColor
parameters.description: Fill color, transparency (default 0.3) and edge color (default "none").

tools.notes: Introduced R2023a. Regions stay fixed relative to data while zooming. Returns ConstantRegion objects.

tools.name: yyaxis
tools.description: Creates an axes with two independent y-axes and selects which side subsequent plotting commands target. Use it to plot two quantities with different units or scales against the same x data.
tools.usage:
yyaxis left
yyaxis right
yyaxis(ax, ___)

parameters.name: left / right
parameters.description: Side to activate for following plot, ylabel, ylim and similar commands.

tools.example:
t = linspace(0, 10, 200);
yyaxis left;  plot(t, sin(t)); ylabel("Voltage (V)")
yyaxis right; plot(t, 100*exp(-t/3)); ylabel("Temperature (\circC)")
xlabel("Time (s)")
tools.notes: Each side cycles through its own color; set ax.YAxis(1).Color to customize. Not supported in some chart types; use tiledlayout for more than two scales.

tools.name: colororder
tools.description: Sets or queries the color order used to color successive plot lines, scatter series and bars in a figure or axes. It accepts an RGB matrix, hex codes or named palettes.
tools.usage:
colororder(colorarray)
colororder(palettename)
colororder(target, ___)
C = colororder
C = colororder(target)

parameters.name: colorarray
parameters.description: m-by-3 RGB matrix, string array of color names or hex codes.

tools.example:
colororder(["#D62728" "#1F77B4" "#2CA02C"])
plot(rand(10,3), LineWidth=2)
colororder(gca, "reef")
tools.notes: Introduced R2019b. Applies to plots created after the call unless the series use automatic SeriesIndex coloring. Use colormap for continuous color mapping instead.

tools.name: datatip
tools.description: Programmatically creates a data tip on a plotted object at a given data point or index. Data tip content can be customized through the object's DataTipTemplate (adding rows with dataTipTextRow).
tools.usage:
dt = datatip(target)
dt = datatip(target, x, y)
dt = datatip(target, x, y, z)
dt = datatip(___, DataIndex=n)
dt = datatip(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Line, Scatter, Surface or other chart object supporting data tips.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: Data location (snaps to nearest vertex by default).

tools.notes: Introduced R2019b. Data tips added this way are exported by exportgraphics. Remove with delete(dt).

tools.name: ginput
tools.description: Lets the user click points in the current axes and returns their coordinates (and which mouse button or key was pressed). Useful for quick manual picking of peaks, regions or calibration points.
tools.usage:
[x, y] = ginput(n)
[x, y] = ginput
[x, y, button] = ginput(___)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of points to collect; without n, collection ends when Return is pressed.

parameters.name: button
parameters.description: Output: 1 left, 2 middle, 3 right mouse button, or ASCII code of a key.

tools.notes: Blocking and interactive: do not use in matlab -batch runs. For draggable, editable selections use drawpoint/drawrectangle (Image Processing Toolbox) or ROI objects.

tools.name: linkaxes
tools.description: Synchronizes the limits of several 2-D axes so that zooming or panning one updates all the others. Typically used with subplots or tiled layouts that share a time axis.
tools.usage:
linkaxes(ax)
linkaxes(ax, dimension)
tools.notes: linkprop links arbitrary properties (e.g. CameraPosition for 3-D views). The limits of the first axes are applied to all when linking.

tools.name: rotate3d
tools.description: Enables or disables interactive 3-D rotation mode in a figure, and returns a mode object for customizing rotation behavior and callbacks.
tools.usage:
rotate3d on
rotate3d off
rotate3d(fig, "on")
h = rotate3d(fig)

parameters.name: h (mode object)
parameters.description: Properties Enable, RotateStyle ("orbit" or "box"), ActionPreCallback, ActionPostCallback.

tools.notes: Axes toolbars provide rotation by default in modern MATLAB; use rotate3d for programmatic control or callbacks. Related modes: zoom, pan, datacursormode, brush.

tools.name: copygraphics
tools.description: Copies a figure, axes, chart or app component to the system clipboard as an image or vector graphic, tightly cropped, ready to paste into documents and presentations.
tools.usage:
copygraphics(target)
copygraphics(target, Name=Value)

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Figure, axes, tiled layout, chart or UI component.

tools.example:
plot(peaks)
copygraphics(gca, ContentType="vector", BackgroundColor="none")
tools.notes: Introduced R2020a. Vector clipboard content is supported on Windows and macOS. Use exportgraphics to write to files with the same options.

tools.name: rectangle
tools.description: Draws a rectangle, rounded rectangle or ellipse in data coordinates of the current axes. Commonly used to mark regions of interest or draw simple shapes and circles.
tools.usage:
rectangle(Position=pos)
rectangle(Position=pos, Curvature=cur)
r = rectangle(ax, ___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: [x y w h] in data units.

parameters.name: Curvature
parameters.description: [horizontal vertical] curvature in [0,1]; [1 1] draws an ellipse.

tools.example:
imagesc(magic(20)); axis image
rectangle(Position=[4 4 6 3], EdgeColor="w", LineWidth=2)
rectangle(Position=[12 12 5 5], Curvature=[1 1], FaceColor=[1 0 0 0.3])
tools.notes: FaceColor accepts a 4-element RGBA vector for transparency. For figure-relative shapes use annotation('rectangle',...).

tools.name: alpha
tools.description: Sets the transparency of surfaces, patches and images in the current axes, either to a constant value or driven by alpha data (per-vertex or per-face transparency).
tools.usage:
alpha(value)
alpha(obj, value)
alpha("flat")
alpha("interp")
alpha("color")

parameters.name: "flat" / "interp" / "color"
parameters.description: Use AlphaData per face, interpolated, or equal to color data.

tools.example:
surf(peaks); hold on
h = surf(peaks + 2);
alpha(h, 0.4)
shading interp
tools.notes: Transparency requires the OpenGL renderer; alim and alphamap control data-to-alpha mapping. For lines use RGBA color vectors.

tools.name: daspect
tools.description: Sets or queries the data aspect ratio of an axes, i.e. the relative scaling of data units along x, y and z. Setting [1 1 1] makes geometric shapes and 3-D objects appear undistorted.
tools.usage:
daspect(ratio)
d = daspect
daspect("auto")
daspect(ax, ___)

parameters.name: ratio
parameters.description: Three-element vector, e.g. [1 1 1] or [1 1 0.2] to exaggerate z.

tools.notes: axis equal sets the data aspect ratio for 2-D plots; pbaspect sets the plot-box aspect ratio instead.

tools.name: fontsize
tools.description: Changes the font size of all text in a figure or graphics object at once (tick labels, labels, titles, legends, UI components), either to an absolute size, by a scale factor, or incrementally.
tools.usage:
fontsize(size, units)
fontsize("increase")
fontsize("decrease")
fontsize(scale=sfactor)
fontsize("default")
fontsize(obj, ___)

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale factor applied to existing sizes.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: Figure or other graphics object (optional since R2023a; defaults to the current figure).

tools.example:
f = figure; plot(rand(5)); legend; title("Results")
fontsize(f, 14, "points")
fontsize(f, scale=1.2)
tools.notes: Introduced R2022a. Handy before exportgraphics for publication figures. fontname similarly changes fonts.

tools.name: uistack
tools.description: Reorders graphics or UI objects in the stacking (drawing) order among their siblings, bringing an object to the front, sending it to the back or moving it by steps.
tools.usage:
uistack(obj)
uistack(obj, opt)
uistack(obj, opt, step)

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Number of levels to move for "up"/"down".

tools.notes: Equivalent to reordering the parent's Children property. In 2-D views with the default SortMethod, stacking order determines visibility.

tools.name: hgtransform
tools.description: Creates a transform group object whose 4x4 Matrix applies translation, rotation and scaling to all of its child graphics objects. It is the efficient way to animate rigid bodies without recomputing vertex data.
tools.usage:
t = hgtransform
t = hgtransform(parent)
t = hgtransform(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Matrix
parameters.description: 4-by-4 homogeneous transform, often built with makehgtform.

tools.notes: makehgtform composes "translate", "scale", "xrotate", "yrotate", "zrotate" and "axisrotate" operations. hggroup groups objects without transforming them.

tools.name: copyobj
tools.description: Copies graphics objects and all their descendants to a new parent, for example to duplicate an axes into another figure or reuse lines in another plot. Callbacks and data are copied, but not the original's listeners.
tools.usage:
newObj = copyobj(obj, parent)
newObj = copyobj(obj, parent, "legacy")

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: New parent object(s), e.g. a figure for an axes or an axes for lines.

parameters.name: "legacy"
parameters.description: Also copy object callback properties and application data as in older releases.

tools.notes: Legends and colorbars are associated objects; copy them together with the axes: copyobj([leg ax], f2). Use tiledlayout + nexttile targets to combine copies into one figure.
